passage: A dictionary of a dying language is rarely the work of a single season. Compiled over more than twenty years from hundreds of recorded interviews with the community's last elderly speakers, ______, and today it stands as the fullest record of a language that has since fallen silent.
question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.text: the last fluent generation was documented by the linguist’s dictionary
documenting the last fluent generation occupied the linguist for many years
the linguist’s dictionary preserved the words of the last fluent generation
there were finally enough recorded words to fill the linguist’s dictionary

explanation: The correct answer is C. The opening phrase, "Compiled over more than twenty years from hundreds of recorded interviews…," must modify the thing that was compiled—the dictionary. Only C makes "the linguist's dictionary" the subject that follows the comma, so the modifier attaches correctly and the later pronoun "it" has a clear antecedent. In A the phrase wrongly describes "the last fluent generation," who were not compiled; in B it points to "documenting," an activity rather than the compiled object; and in D the dummy "there were" leaves the introductory phrase with nothing sensible to modify.
